doubts.note: Sections titled with a translator's name (Nott, Macgregor, Wrangham, Capel Lofft, Charlemont, Wollaston, Merivale, Anon., Ox., 1795, and their -2, -3 ... variants, about 170 sections) are second translations of the sonnet before them: the source prints each translation's signature (NOTT., MACGREGOR.) after it, and the script took the signature as the heading of the next translation. The texts are complete; only the titles are wrong. Left alone.

doubts.note: the sections titled By Lope de Vega, By Francisco de Aldana, Anonymous, By Gonzalo de Berceo, By Santa Teresa de Avila, By Diego de Saldana, By Cristobal de Castillejo, By El Commendador Escriva are titled from the attribution line under the real title (The Good Shepherd, To-morrow, Santa Teresa's Book-Mark, ...). stanza 2 (Worn with speed is my good steed) is a second song in the same scene; keep_stanzas [0,1] keeps only the first song.
stanza 3 (The nuns in the cloister) is the same song heard dying away, after two lines of dialogue; keep_stanzas [0,1,2] follows the example given and drops it.
sections Postscript, Postscript-2, Postscript-3 are verse postscripts to epistles, cut from their epistles; genuine verse, left alone.

the line Come out along wi' us, an' fling up thy heels appears twice in this section (stanzas 4 and 8) and is the last line before the eclogue The Veairies in the source; the section may itself contain a second poem. Not checked.

the eclogue The Times (John an' Tom, Well, Tom, how be'st?) is also in no section; recorded with The Veairies. Section the-common-a-took-in is the song of that name, not the eclogue The Common a-took in (John and Thomas), whose text was not located.

sections argeia, in-alas-alas, artemis, poem-ii, ode-3 (SPK flags, hundreds of lines with speaker tags) are almost certainly more of the masks Prometheus the Firegiver and Demeter; only prometheus, servant, inachus and dramatis-person-2 were checked and recorded.
the source heading ELEGY stands 55 lines after this section's first line (Clear and gentle stream!); the four 12-line stanzas may belong to a different poem. Not resolved.
sections warrior, warrior-2, indian, indian-4 and the like are speeches of a dramatic poem cut at speaker headings, as in Barnes; not mapped.
whether stanza 4 (It is not far, it is not near) is still the song or already dialogue was not checked; keep_stanzas [0-4] assumes it is the song.
